headline: Simple decoders recover visual images from primate spikes; RL networks mimic decisions
label: Neural Coding And Decoding Models
summary: Decoding benchmarks and learned recurrent decision models now offer testable links between spiking activity, perception, and behavior.
synthesis: The dominant thread is relating neural activity to perception and behavior through explicitly specified computational models. A systematic evaluation of decoding visual images from primate intracortical spiking data finds that a simple temporal-attention plus MLP model reaches 70% top-1 retrieval, suggesting that modest architectures can recover rich representational content. A separate preprint trains recurrent networks with deep reinforcement learning on a noisy task and reports primate-like speed-accuracy tradeoffs and changes of mind with neural-like dynamics. A published mouse study tests higher-level spatial prediction in natural vision within predictive processing theory. What is new is the pairing of decoding benchmarks with learned recurrent models of decision making. The three items differ in method, an empirical benchmark, a simulation-based learning study, and a test of theory, so the shared thread is conceptual rather than methodological.
